item.title: At a small music venue
item.description: Learn how to talk about getting ready to play a local show and what happens when you go to see one.

children.definition: A place where an organised event such as a concert takes place.
children.example: The band chose a small venue near the station so friends could come by train.

children.definition: A practice session before a performance.
children.example: At rehearsal, we played the last song three times to get the ending right.

children.definition: The area where musicians or other performers stand or sit while people watch them.
children.example: Someone brought out a chair and put it in the middle of the stage for the guitarist.
Our drummer counted to four, and we all started playing together.

children.definition: To adjust a musical instrument so that it produces the correct notes.
children.example: I tuned my guitar in the hall while the room was still quiet.

children.definition: A device used to pick up a voice or another sound so it can be made louder or recorded.
children.example: The singer held the microphone out so we could sing the last line with her.

children.definition: A performer or group that plays before the main performer or group at a show.
children.example: The opening act was a singer from our neighbourhood who played her own songs.
children.translation_uz: asosiy chiqishdan oldin sahnaga chiqadigan ijrochi yoki guruh
collocations: the opening act for a band

children.definition: A line of people waiting for their turn.
children.example: We joined the queue outside just as someone came to open the doors.

children.definition: If a show does this, people buy all the available tickets.
children.example: We bought tickets early because Saturday shows often sell out.
children.translation_ru: о концерте или другом мероприятии: все билеты на него распродаются

children.definition: The line of seats closest to the people performing.
children.example: We sat in the front row and could see the guitarist's fingers clearly.
collocations: a seat in the front row

children.definition: The sound of people clapping to show that they enjoyed something.
children.example: The applause was so loud that we could barely hear the singer say thank you.

children.definition: An extra performance of one or more pieces at the end of a show, usually because the audience wants to hear more.
children.example: People kept clapping, so the band came back and played an encore.
children.translation_uz: konsert oxirida, odatda tomoshabinlar iltimosiga koʻra, bir yoki bir nechta asarning qoʻshimcha ijro etilishi

children.definition: A series of songs or pieces musicians perform one after another in one part of a show.
children.example: We started our second set with a slow song and finished with something people could dance to.
children.translation_ru: блок песен или пьес в рамках одного выступления
children.translation_uz: ketma-ket ijro etiladigan qoʻshiq yoki kuylardan iborat konsert boʻlimi

children.definition: A strip worn around the wrist to show that someone is allowed into an event or area.
children.example: The volunteer gave me a blue wristband so I could go outside and come back in between bands.
